invariants.description: Merchant organization and outlet authority is derived from the authenticated account and current active membership.
Request-supplied organization and outlet identifiers are validated targets, never authority.
Current membership, permission, and outlet status are re-evaluated for online and replayed commands.
Spring Boot and PostgreSQL remain canonical inventory authority.
Normal inventory mutations create commands and immutable movements instead of setting client stock.
Canonical inventory always satisfies onHand >= reserved >= 0.
Retrying an accepted command cannot duplicate its business effect.
Reusing a command key with a different request fingerprint fails closed.
Contested inventory has one database-ordered winner.
Local persistence is cache, operational state, and durable queue rather than marketplace authority.
The UI reports synced only after durable application of a server receipt.
Process death cannot lose a locally acknowledged command.
Unsynchronized Merchant changes are never exposed as canonical Customer state.
Quote and checkout reload listing, price, outlet, commerce mode, and available inventory.
Supported barcodes remain strings, preserve leading zeroes, and validate GTIN checksums.
Barcode payloads never supply ownership, price, stock, tax, or authenticity.
Canonical money remains integer paise.
Medicine remains compatible with canonical VIEW_ONLY restrictions.
Normal CRUD cannot destroy inventory, commerce, financial, loyalty, or audit history.
V1 cannot finalize a POS sale while fully offline.
Applied Flyway migrations are immutable and schema changes use new forward migrations.
Skipped, focused, fabricated, or unexecuted tests cannot satisfy a merge gate.
